question: What does professional autonomy mean for a modern clinical nurse?

options.B: Making independent, accountable clinical decisions within one's scope of practice
options.C: Refusing to follow hospital administrative policies or protocols
options.D: Prescribing major pharmaceutical drugs without medical supervision

explanation: Exactly! Autonomy means having the confidence and professional right to make sound clinical choices within your training limits. [learn more](GST321_U8_T7#GST321_U8_T7_h5)

question: How should a nurse first care for an exposed spinal sac on a newborn with spina bifida cystica?

options.A: Leave it wide open to the air to dry out
options.B: Apply tight plaster bandages over the area
options.C: Wash the nerves gently with antiseptic soap
options.D: Apply a sterile, moist saline dressing and keep baby off their back

explanation: We want to keep that delicate tissue moist and safe from infection, while making sure the baby lies on their side or tummy so there's no pressure on the sac. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T020#GNS226_U3_T020_h6)

question: Why might a breastfeeding mother be given a progestin-only pill instead of a combined pill?

options.A: Minipills taste better for the baby
options.B: Estrogen can decrease the breast milk supply
options.C: Progestin stops milk production completely
options.D: Combined pills cause infant colic

explanation: Great clinical thinking! Estrogen in combined pills can negatively affect milk production, so we prefer progestin-only options (minipills) to keep breastfeeding going strong. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T012#GNS226_U6_T012_h1)

question: What is the surgery called when a badly damaged joint is completely replaced with an artificial one?

options.A: Arthroscopy
options.B: Arthrodesis
options.C: Osteotomy
options.D: Arthroplasty

explanation: Spot on! Arthroplasty is the medical term for joint replacement surgery using modern metal and plastic implants. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T13#GNS222_U1_T13_h7)

question: How does close communication between nurses and family caregivers impact client care?

options.A: It ensures consistency between care practices at the center and at home
options.B: It prevents the nursing staff from making independent clinical choices
options.C: It creates unnecessary confusion and conflicting daily schedules
options.D: It allows the family to completely delegate all thinking to the staff

explanation: Sharing observations and strategies between home and the facility creates a unified approach that benefits the client's stability and comfort. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T7#GNS324_U5_T7_h7)

question: Which nursing action directly helps prevent deep vein thrombosis in a patient on bedrest?

options.A: Encouraging early ambulation and leg exercises
options.B: Massaging the calf muscles firmly to break up small clots
options.C: Applying warm heating pads directly over the fracture site
options.D: Keeping the injured limb elevated above heart level all day

explanation: Movement is medicine! When muscles contract, they act like a pump pushing blood back to the heart, stopping it from pooling and forming clots. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T23#GNS222_U1_T23_h9)

question: What is the main body purpose of warning signs like pain and fever?

options.A: To act as warning signals indicating internal distress or disease
options.B: To punish the patient for eating unhealthy foods
options.C: To slow down normal blood circulation in the limbs
options.D: To increase the body weight of an infected person

explanation: Exactly! Think of pain and fever as the body's alarm system alerting you that something inside needs attention. [learn more](GNS215_U4_T4#GNS215_U4_T4_h6)

question: What are the three core principles of radiation safety?

options.A: Time, distance, and shielding
options.B: Light, sound, and pressure
options.C: Color, weight, and volume
options.D: Speed, heat, and moisture

explanation: Limiting exposure time, increasing distance from the source, and using physical shielding protect workers from harmful radiation. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T7#GNS112_U4_T7_h6)

question: If you want to attend a learning session focused strictly on practicing physical skills with supervision, which one should you pick?

options.A: A workshop
options.B: A conference
options.C: A lecture series
options.D: A seminar

explanation: Workshops are all about action! Instead of just sitting and listening, you get your hands dirty practicing procedures under the watchful eye of an expert. [learn more](GST321_U8_T8#GST321_U8_T8_h3)

question: What is the primary purpose of regular pacemaker interrogation appointments?

options.A: To surgically replace the battery every six months
options.B: To reprogram the heart muscle to beat much faster
options.C: To check battery life and evaluate device functioning
options.D: To wash the surgical scar and apply fresh bandages

explanation: Interrogation allows healthcare providers to assess remaining battery power, lead performance, and device data. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T9#GNS321_U2_T9_h8)

question: A patient on strong pain medication reports feeling constantly queasy and unable to keep food down. What is the nurse's best initial action?

options.A: Administer a strong laxative immediately to clear the bowels
options.B: Identify the specific trigger to select the correct antiemetic
options.C: Force the patient to finish a standard hospital meal tray
options.D: Advise the patient to completely stop drinking all water

explanation: Different antiemetics work on different pathways in the body, so finding the cause ensures the right medication is given. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T15#GNS321_U4_T15_h3)

question: When talking to a patient with GPI, what speech and facial sign might you notice?

options.A: They cannot make any sound at all.
options.B: They stutter rapidly only when they are stressed.
options.C: Slurred speech with trembling around the lips.
options.D: They suddenly switch to speaking a foreign language.

explanation: Spot on! Nerve damage affects the tiny muscles of the mouth and tongue, causing mild tremors and classic slurred speech. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T1#GNS222_U4_T1_h3)

question: Why must nurses work to eliminate personal bias regarding gender roles in the clinic?

options.A: Hospital management requires all nurses to pass a gender exam
options.B: Biases prevent nurses from dispensing medications properly
options.C: Ministry of health guidelines ban nurses from talking to men
options.D: Biased attitudes can make men feel unwelcome and drive them away from care

explanation: When nurses act judgmentally or ignore fathers, it reinforces the belief that health clinics are not meant for men. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T58#GNS214_U1_T58_h7)

question: Why is it so important to accurately chart the exact time and volume of a blood transfusion?

options.A: It provides a legal record of care and helps track fluid balance
options.B: It prevents the patient from receiving another transfusion ever again
options.C: It is only required for hospital billing and insurance purposes
options.D: It allows the nurse to claim overtime payment for the procedure

explanation: Good charting keeps your patient safe and protects your license! It gives a clear picture of their fluid status and serves as a legal record that you delivered safe, quality care. [learn more](GNS311_U2_T12#GNS311_U2_T12_h7)

question: What is the primary goal of routine screening tests like the Pap smear?

options.A: To permanently cure active bacterial infections in the pelvis
options.B: To detect abnormal cellular changes before cancer develops
options.C: To prevent the initial transmission of sexually transmitted germs
options.D: To measure hormone levels during the normal menstrual cycle

explanation: Pap smears catch weird cellular changes early—long before they turn into cancer—making treatment quick and easy. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T3#GNS216_U1_T3_h7)

question: What is the main goal of surgical asepsis?

options.A: To kill all viruses while leaving bacteria alive
options.B: To reduce the total number of common bacteria
options.C: To eliminate every single microorganism and spore
options.D: To remove visible dirt and grease from the skin

explanation: You've got this! Surgical asepsis is all about absolute sterility—getting rid of every living germ and tough spore so nothing can cause infection. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T3#GNS123_U5_T3_h1)

question: Which quick bedside test should a nurse perform immediately for any patient presenting with sudden confusion?

options.A: Blood glucose test
options.B: Chest X-ray imaging
options.C: Electrocardiogram test
options.D: Complete blood count

explanation: Low blood sugar is a common, easily reversible cause of altered mental status that must be checked right away. [learn more](GNS315_U2_T2#GNS315_U2_T2_h6)

question: Why is checking for an intact hymen an unreliable way to judge someone's sexual history?

options.A: It is absent in more than half of all healthy females at birth.
options.B: It disappears completely in all females prior to puberty.
options.C: It can be stretched or torn by non-sexual activities like exercise.
options.D: It regenerates rapidly after any form of physical trauma.

explanation: Important clinical point! Everyday activities like sports, stretching, or using tampons can alter the hymen without any sexual contact. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T1#GNS121_U5_T1_h6)

question: Why do we sometimes treat a dry, hacking cough with medicine, even though coughing is a natural body defense?

options.A: It prevents oxygen from reaching the brain tissues.
options.B: It stops the heart from beating too fast during sleep.
options.C: It always indicates a permanent lung collapse.
options.D: It causes tiredness and chest pain without bringing up any phlegm.

explanation: A dry cough doesn't help clear anything out—it just leaves your patient exhausted and sore. Treating it helps them get some much-needed rest! [learn more](GNS223_U2_T1#GNS223_U2_T1_h1)

question: Which of these makes an infection show up much faster (shortens the incubation period)?

options.A: Strong baseline immunity in the host
options.B: Slow replication rate of the pathogen
options.C: A very high initial infectious dose
options.D: Superficial entry through intact skin

explanation: Correct! If a huge number of germs enter your body at once, they don't need as much time to multiply before making you sick. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T9#GNS313_U1_T9_h3)

question: What exciting new skill does an infant show when they develop a pincer grasp?

options.A: Support the entire weight of the body on the legs
options.B: Pick up small objects using the thumb and index finger
options.C: Roll over from the abdomen to the back easily
options.D: Hold a heavy feeding bottle without any assistance

explanation: Exactly! The pincer grasp is a fun milestone where baby uses their thumb and index finger like tiny tweezers to grab small bits of food. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T12#GNS324_U3_T12_h2)

question: What type of immune reaction causes the raised bump during a Mantoux test?

options.A: Immediate antibody production
options.B: Complement system activation
options.C: Cell-mediated hypersensitivity
options.D: Innate inflammatory defense

explanation: Think of this as your immune cells (T-cells) rushing to the spot and throwing a little party that takes a day or two to show up as a firm lump! [learn more](GNS213_U5_T12#GNS213_U5_T12_h2)

question: What is the primary purpose of a Glucose Tolerance Test?

options.A: To measure how the body clears a glucose load over time
options.B: To evaluate how quickly the kidneys filter sugar from the blood
options.C: To measure the exact amount of insulin stored in the pancreas
options.D: To determine the average blood sugar level over the past three months

explanation: The GTT tracks how effectively the body processes and clears a specific amount of glucose over several hours. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T20#GNS222_U2_T20_h1)

question: How do beta-blockers help a patient diagnosed with coronary artery disease?

options.A: By dissolving existing blood clots inside the narrowed arteries
options.B: By increasing the strength of every single heart contraction
options.C: By widening the peripheral blood vessels in the legs and arms
options.D: By slowing the heart rate and reducing the heart's oxygen demand

explanation: Beta-blockers block adrenaline effects on the heart, lowering heart rate and blood pressure so the heart muscle needs less oxygen. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T4#GNS213_U1_T4_h6)

question: Which layer of the placenta is directly bathed in the mother's blood?

options.A: Fetal endothelium
options.B: Connective tissue
options.C: Syncytiotrophoblast
options.D: Cytotrophoblast

explanation: The syncytiotrophoblast is the brave outer layer that sits right in the maternal blood pool, handling nutrient and gas exchange for the baby. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T5#GNS121_U6_T5_h2)

question: Which of the following is NOT a core responsibility of a community health nurse in immunization programs?

options.A: Educating mothers on the schedule of routine immunizations
options.B: Tracking children who default on their vaccination doses
options.C: Manufacturing synthetic vaccine formulas in the local clinic
options.D: Administering vaccines safely while maintaining cold chain

explanation: Nurses administer, educate, and track patients, but vaccine manufacturing happens in specialized pharmaceutical laboratories, not local clinics. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T8#GNS313_U1_T8_h8)

question: Why is enteral tube feeding preferred over parenteral nutrition when the digestive tract works?

options.A: It delivers pure water without any dissolved nutrients
options.B: It requires no monitoring of blood glucose levels
options.C: It preserves gut function and protects the intestinal lining
options.D: It carries zero risk of infection or mechanical blockage

explanation: Using the gastrointestinal tract keeps the gut mucosa healthy and prevents bacterial translocation, making enteral feeding the safer choice. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T009#GNS227_U6_T009_h7)

question: Which factor is a major warning sign for nutritional risk in hospitalized patients?

options.A: Involuntary weight loss
options.B: Sleeping on the left side
options.C: Preferring sweet drinks
options.D: Wearing loose clothing

explanation: Unplanned or involuntary weight loss is one of the strongest indicators that a patient is at high risk for malnutrition. [learn more](GNS227_U5_T001#GNS227_U5_T001_h3)

question: Which type of cervical traction involves putting metal pins directly into the skull bone?

options.A: Manual traction
options.B: Halter traction
options.C: Skin traction
options.D: Halo traction

explanation: Great job! Skeletal traction (like a halo device) uses metal pins right in the bone so it can handle much stronger pulling forces. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T12#GNS221_U1_T12_h2)

question: What is a major benefit of steaming veggies instead of boiling them in lots of water?

options.A: It prevents valuable water-soluble vitamins from leaching out into the cooking water
options.B: It stops the food from ever spoiling during long hospital storage
options.C: It doubles the amount of protein found in leafy green vegetables
options.D: It completely eliminates all natural plant sugars from the food

explanation: Spot on! Steaming uses just a little steam, locking those precious vitamins safely inside the food instead of pouring them down the sink. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T004#GNS227_U4_T004_h4)

question: Why should you do a quick physical assessment right after the steam session ends?

options.A: To check if the bed linens need washing
options.B: To evaluate how well the treatment worked
options.C: To see if the patient needs a snack or drink
options.D: To make sure the electrical cord is cool

explanation: Spot on! Comparing your notes now with your baseline check tells you if the therapy did its job. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T8#GNS212_U2_T8_h7)

question: Why is starting ORT right at home so important for community health?

options.A: It eliminates the need for any professional medical checkups
options.B: It prevents family members from catching the same stomach bug
options.C: It guarantees that the underlying viral infection will disappear overnight
options.D: It stops dehydration from progressing to a dangerous stage before reaching a clinic

explanation: Every minute counts! Giving fluids immediately at home stops mild fluid loss from turning into a life-threatening emergency before the family even reaches the hospital. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T57#GNS214_U1_T57_h8)

question: Why is it important for nurses to look beyond purely physical complaints when checking for depression?

options.A: Patients will always directly report feeling sad without prompting
options.B: Physical complaints always disappear once mental health improves
options.C: Depression frequently presents itself disguised as chronic pain or fatigue
options.D: Physical symptoms are completely unrelated to psychological health

explanation: Great job! Patients often show up with body aches, headaches, or extreme tiredness rather than saying they feel sad. Staying alert to this helps us catch what's really going on. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T2#GNS324_U4_T2_h1)

question: What can happen if a breastfeeding mother drastically cuts her calories to lose weight too fast?

options.A: It stops the infant from sleeping
options.B: It can reduce the daily milk supply
options.C: It causes permanent bone density loss
options.D: It changes the baby's blood type

explanation: Crash dieting sends a signal to the body to slow down and conserve energy, which can unfortunately cause your milk supply to drop. Slow and steady wins the race! [learn more](GNS227_U2_T013#GNS227_U2_T013_h2)

question: What do we call the entire group of people a researcher actually wants to study?

options.A: Population
options.B: Parameter
options.C: Variable
options.D: Sample

explanation: That's correct! The 'population' is the total group you are interested in—like all diabetic patients in Lagos State. Keep up the great flow! [learn more](GNS217_U4_T3#GNS217_U4_T3_h2)

question: What is the correct nursing action when a mentally competent adult client refuses a prescribed blood transfusion?

options.A: Respect the refusal, educate the client on the risks, and notify the attending doctor
options.B: Threaten to discharge the client immediately from the hospital ward
options.C: Call security officers to hold the client down during the procedure
options.D: Administer the blood transfusion secretly while the client is sleeping

explanation: Competent adults have the right to refuse treatment, and nurses must document this while informing the medical team. [learn more](GST321_U10_T5#GST321_U10_T5_h4)

question: Why is a urinary catheter put in place when treating a patient in severe shock from bleeding?

options.A: To stop the patient from moving around in bed
options.B: To empty the bladder before a surgical procedure
options.C: To collect a clean-catch urine culture specimen
options.D: To monitor hourly urine output to check kidney function

explanation: Urine output is a fantastic mirror for how well the kidneys and vital organs are receiving blood during resuscitation. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T008#GNS226_U5_T008_h3)

question: What happens right away during the emission phase?

options.A: Urine is forced out of the kidneys
options.B: Semen gathers in the prostatic urethra
options.C: The external sphincter permanently relaxes
options.D: Sperm are newly created in the bladder

explanation: Emission is just the gathering step—sperm and fluids team up and wait in the upper urethra before the big push outward! [learn more](GNS121_U4_T5#GNS121_U4_T5_h3)

question: A patient having a severe asthma attack gets an intravenous steroid. What is the main goal of giving this in an emergency?

options.A: To thin out thick mucus plugs blocking the lower lung passages
options.B: To immediately relax tightened smooth muscle bands around the windpipe
options.C: To boost the patient's heart rate and increase oxygen delivery
options.D: To reduce swelling and inflammation inside the bronchial airways

explanation: Remember, steroids take a little time to change gene expression, so they aren't quick-fix muscle relaxers—they are used to bring down the dangerous swelling inside the airways. [learn more](GNS223_U7_T4#GNS223_U7_T4_h3)

question: Which of these is NOT a warning sign of a pelvic infection after a procedure?

options.A: Foul-smelling or purulent vaginal discharge
options.B: Severe and worsening lower abdominal pain
options.C: Persistent fever and chills
options.D: Sudden development of normal morning appetite

explanation: Spot on! Wanting to eat normally is a sign of a happy, healing body. Fever, bad-smelling discharge, and terrible pain are the real warning signs to watch out for. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T5#GNS311_U1_T5_h8)

question: Which of these options has NO effect on how well your body absorbs nutrients?

options.A: The health and integrity of the villi
options.B: The pH of the digestive tract
options.C: Intestinal motility speed
options.D: The astrological sign of the patient

explanation: Haha, definitely not your horoscope! Nutrient absorption depends strictly on physical and chemical factors like gut movement, pH, and mucosal health. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T7#GNS121_U1_T7_h6)

question: What is a major physical danger for children who hawk items on busy Nigerian highways?

options.A: Chronic occupational asthma
options.B: Severe radiation sickness
options.C: Degenerative joint disease
options.D: Road traffic accidents

explanation: Exactly! Weaving through moving cars to sell goods puts children at high risk of being hit by vehicles. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T3#GNS225_U5_T3_h4)

question: What is the go-to emergency medication for a patient in acute anaphylactic shock?

options.A: Epinephrine
options.B: Salbutamol inhaler
options.C: Diphenhydramine
options.D: Hydrocortisone

explanation: Epinephrine is a lifesaver in anaphylaxis! It quickly tightens blood vessels, opens up tight airways, and keeps the heart pumping. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T6#GNS112_U7_T6_h6)

question: Where is the best anatomical site to inject emergency epinephrine?

options.A: Gluteal muscle
options.B: Mid-outer thigh
options.C: Subcutaneous abdomen
options.D: Deltoid muscle

explanation: The vastus lateralis (mid-outer thigh) absorbs epinephrine the fastest into the bloodstream. Plus, you can even give it right through trousers in a rush! [learn more](GST114_U4_T9#GST114_U4_T9_h5)

question: A patient collapses in the hospital ward. What should the nurse do right after confirming the patient is unresponsive and not breathing normally?

options.A: Leave the patient to find a doctor
options.B: Call for help and activate the emergency response
options.C: Administer rescue breaths through a mask
options.D: Start chest compressions immediately

explanation: Activating the emergency team immediately ensures that extra hands and equipment like an AED are on the way. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T1#GNS212_U2_T1_h3)

question: Which medication is typically prescribed as the first-line oral treatment for Type 2 diabetes?

options.A: Regular insulin
options.B: NPH insulin
options.C: Metformin
options.D: Glibenclamide

explanation: Metformin is universally recommended as the starting oral drug because it lowers blood sugar effectively without causing weight gain or low blood sugar on its own. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T13#GNS214_U1_T13_h4)

question: Why do nurses need to handle strong chemical sterilants like glutaraldehyde with extra care?

options.A: They instantly blow up under bright theatre lamps
options.B: They can cause bad skin rashes, irritation, and breathing trouble
options.C: They completely cancel out the local anaesthetic given to patients
options.D: They melt stainless steel instruments into liquid on contact

explanation: Potent disinfectants are harsh on living cells! We always need good ventilation and protective gear to keep these chemicals away from our skin and lungs. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T12#GNS123_U5_T12_h4)

question: What is a major strength of using explanatory research in healthcare?

options.A: They require zero effort to plan and execute
options.B: They allow researchers to skip informed consent
options.C: They completely eliminate all hospital financial costs
options.D: They provide clear evidence for clinical interventions

explanation: Spot on! The biggest win of explanatory research is generating solid evidence to upgrade patient care. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T13#GNS224_U1_T13_h8)

question: How do diuretic medications help bring down high blood pressure?

options.A: By helping the kidneys remove excess sodium and water
options.B: By blocking calcium entry into arterial wall cells
options.C: By strengthening the pumping force of the left ventricle
options.D: By directly slowing down the electrical conduction of the heart

explanation: Diuretics are 'water pills'! They tell the kidneys to flush out extra salt and water, shrinking the total fluid volume in the pipes so pressure drops. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T6#GNS111_U2_T6_h7)

question: Why are both FSH and testosterone needed for normal sperm production in males?

options.A: Because both hormones are actually identical chemical substances made by the liver
options.B: Because FSH supports the supporting cells while testosterone drives the overall development
options.C: Because testosterone fights off infections while FSH controls body temperature
options.D: Because FSH stops the growth of body hair while testosterone makes bones brittle

explanation: Exactly right! FSH supports the helper cells (Sertoli cells), while testosterone provides the fuel needed for sperm cells to fully mature. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T13#GNS121_U5_T13_h5)

question: Why are older adults much more likely to experience bad side effects from medications?

options.A: They always forget to swallow their pills with water
options.B: Their stomach acid completely destroys all medications
options.C: Their bodies metabolize and excrete medications much slower
options.D: They prefer taking herbal remedies instead of real drugs

explanation: Because liver and kidney functions slow down with age, drugs hang around in the body much longer. If doses aren't adjusted, they can easily build up to toxic levels. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T3#GNS324_U3_T3_h6)

question: A patient admits they smoke too much, but they have zero plans to quit anytime soon. Which stage of change are they in?

options.A: Preparation
options.B: Maintenance
options.C: Precontemplation
options.D: Contemplation

explanation: In precontemplation, a person isn't ready to change yet and might not even see a problem with their habit. It's our job as nurses to meet them where they are with patience! [learn more](GNS225_U2_T27#GNS225_U2_T27_h2)

question: Which socio-cultural factor most commonly discourages men from seeking early healthcare?

options.A: Lack of available male doctors
options.B: Strict government hospital regulations
options.C: Fear of paying high transport costs
options.D: Viewing health-seeking behavior as a sign of weakness

explanation: Traditional definitions of masculinity often make men hide illness or delay seeking help to appear strong. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T58#GNS214_U1_T58_h2)

question: Which route of administration is best for treating a sudden, life-threatening allergic reaction?

options.A: Inhaled powder
options.B: Oral tablet
options.C: Topical cream
options.D: Intravenous

explanation: Spot on! The intravenous (IV) route pushes the medication straight into the bloodstream for instant action during emergencies. [learn more](GNS223_U5_T3#GNS223_U5_T3_h3)

question: A patient recovered from typhoid fever weeks ago, but lab tests still show they are shedding the bacteria. What type of carrier are they?

options.A: A chronic carrier
options.B: A clinical case
options.C: A healthy carrier
options.D: A convalescent carrier

explanation: Great job thinking this through! Someone who continues to carry and shed germs long after recovering from the illness is known as a chronic carrier. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T7#GNS313_U1_T7_h2)

question: During the early (compensated) stage of shock, why do the skin and limbs often feel cool and pale?

options.A: Red blood cells lose their oxygen-carrying capacity in peripheral tissues
options.B: The ambient room temperature directly lowers the peripheral skin temperature
options.C: Blood is shunted away from non-vital areas to protect the heart and brain
options.D: Superficial blood vessels dilate to release excess heat from the body core

explanation: Think of the body as a smart manager: when resources are low, it redirects blood away from the skin and tummy to keep vital organs like the heart and brain happy. That's why the hands and feet get cool and pale first! [learn more](GNS112_U7_T3#GNS112_U7_T3_h2)

question: A patient steps onto the clinic scale wearing heavy leather boots and a thick jacket. What should the nurse do?

options.A: Subtract two kilograms manually in your head and record that number
options.B: Proceed with the measurement as is since clothing weight does not matter
options.C: Ask the patient to remove the boots and heavy jacket before weighing
options.D: Refuse to measure the patient until another day

explanation: Heavy shoes and clothes add extra weight to the scale. Asking the patient to take them off gives you a true and accurate reading! [learn more](GNS112_U6_T3#GNS112_U6_T3_h2)

question: How does hyperemesis gravidarum differ from normal pregnancy morning sickness?

options.A: It only occurs during the final trimester of pregnancy
options.B: It causes severe, unstoppable vomiting leading to dehydration and weight loss
options.C: It has no effect on the overall fluid balance of the body
options.D: It usually resolves completely within the first four weeks

explanation: While normal morning sickness is manageable, hyperemesis involves nonstop vomiting that drains the body's fluids and nutrition. Great job keeping the clinical differences clear! [learn more](GNS226_U2_T016#GNS226_U2_T016_h1)

question: Why is keeping accurate records of swab counts so important for Nigerian nurses?

options.A: It provides legal protection and proves adherence to safety standards
options.B: It replaces the need to count out loud in the theater
options.C: It allows the hospital to buy fewer supplies next year
options.D: It is only required for hospital billing departments

explanation: Good paperwork is your best backup! Clear records show you followed all safety rules and protect you legally. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T7#GNS123_U5_T7_h6)

question: A community midwife discovers that local TBAs frequently perform dangerous abdominal massage on women in labor. What is the most appropriate initial action?

options.A: Ignore the practice since traditional customs cannot be changed
options.B: Engage the TBAs in training sessions to explain the risks and teach safe referral habits
options.C: Open a competing private hospital directly across the village square
options.D: Call the police to arrest every traditional birth attendant in the village immediately

explanation: Collaborative training respectful dialogue is far more effective at stopping harmful practices than outright hostility or alienation. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T14#GNS225_U3_T14_h7)

question: Why is 24-hour accountability so important in primary nursing?

options.A: It ensures consistent, uninterrupted planning and evaluation of patient care across all shifts.
options.B: It forces the primary nurse to stay awake in the hospital for a full day and night.
options.C: It guarantees that physicians do not need to visit the patient after admission.
options.D: It prevents associate nurses from ever touching the patient or charting notes.

explanation: Don't worry, nurses don't stay awake 24 hours! 24-hour accountability means the primary nurse sets the master plan so that even when they go home to rest, other shifts follow that same smooth path. [learn more](GNS123_U1_T3#GNS123_U1_T3_h2)

question: A clinic manager uses past registers to estimate how many malaria test kits to order next. What does this show?

options.A: Ensuring compliance with tax laws
options.B: Providing evidence for prosecuting staff
options.C: Forecasting medical supplies and preventing stockouts
options.D: Assessing individual nursing licensure

explanation: Looking at past numbers helps clinics predict what they'll need tomorrow. That way, you never run out of essential test kits when a patient walks in! [learn more](GNS124_U6_T2#GNS124_U6_T2_h2)

question: Why do nurse educators love using scenario-based multiple-choice questions instead of plain memorization questions?

options.A: They eliminate the need to teach pathophysiology in the classroom.
options.B: They test higher-order thinking and application rather than just memorization.
options.C: They ensure every student achieves a passing grade automatically.
options.D: They take significantly less time for students to read and answer.

explanation: Scenario questions challenge you to think like a real nurse handling a patient situation, which is way more practical than just cramming definitions! [learn more](GST321_U9_T3#GST321_U9_T3_h3)

question: A 16-year-old first-time pregnant girl comes to her first antenatal visit. How should the nurse behave to make sure she comes back?

options.A: Offering a friendly, confidential environment free from moral judgment
options.B: Requiring an older family member to answer all questions for her
options.C: Limiting her visit duration to avoid overwhelming her with information
options.D: Scolding her gently for becoming pregnant at such a young age

explanation: Teens often avoid clinics because they fear being scolded or judged. A warm, welcoming, and confidential space builds real trust! [learn more](GNS225_U6_T6#GNS225_U6_T6_h7)

question: Why is being kind and compassionate so important when caring for a PAC patient?

options.A: It prevents the physical pain caused by uterine contractions
options.B: It shortens the standard hospital stay to less than two hours
options.C: It completely eliminates the need for any antibiotic therapy
options.D: It reduces anxiety and encourages honest disclosure of medical history

explanation: When patients feel safe and free from judgment, they are much more likely to share true details that help us care for them better. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T025#GNS226_U5_T025_h1)

question: You notice tidaling has suddenly stopped in the water seal chamber of a stable patient. What should you check first?

options.A: Check the tubing for kinks, blockages, or loops hanging too low
options.B: Call the surgeon to request immediate removal of the chest tube
options.C: Disconnect the drainage system from the wall suction source
options.D: Immediately clamp the chest tube with two heavy metal hemostats

explanation: Don't panic! When tidaling stops, it often just means something is blocking the tube, like a kink or a loop resting under the bed. Check the lines first. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T15#GNS213_U2_T15_h5)

question: Which test gives doctors the final, definitive confirmation that a patient has lung cancer?

options.A: Pulmonary function test
options.B: Tissue biopsy
options.C: Routine chest X-ray
options.D: Complete blood count

explanation: Spot on! Scans can strongly suggest cancer, but a pathologist needs to look at an actual tissue sample under a microscope to confirm it. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T11#GNS313_U3_T11_h4)

question: Why do our hands and face get a much larger area on the sensory homunculus than our back or thighs?

options.A: They are closer physically to the brain
options.B: They contain larger bones and thicker muscles
options.C: They receive more blood flow from the carotid arteries
options.D: They have a much higher density of sensory receptors

explanation: Spot on! Areas of the body we use for fine, detailed feeling (like fingertips and lips) have way more receptors, so the brain gives them extra processing space. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T28#GNS211_U3_T28_h6)

question: What is the main reason we give antibiotic eye ointment to a newborn right after birth?

options.A: Lubricating dry eyes caused by bright delivery lights
options.B: Preventing ophthalmia neonatorum from birth canal infections
options.C: Treating congenital cataracts and visual impairments
options.D: Preventing viral conjunctivitis acquired from nursery staff

explanation: This routine ointment protects the baby's eyes from nasty bacteria like gonorrhea or chlamydia that they might pick up while passing through the birth canal. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T011#GNS226_U3_T011_h4)

question: When is a strong purgative commonly used in a clinical setting?

options.A: Replacing lost electrolytes after severe dehydration
options.B: Clearing the bowel before a colonoscopy or surgery
options.C: Lowering high fever during a malaria infection
options.D: Treating severe bacterial infections in the bloodstream

explanation: You're doing great! Strong purgatives are standard practice for cleaning out the intestinal tract before medical scopes or operations. [learn more](GNS223_U3_T2#GNS223_U3_T2_h6)

question: Why do sprained ligaments usually take a long time to heal?

options.A: Ligaments are constantly exposed to air
options.B: Ligaments lack any nerve endings to signal repair
options.C: Ligaments have a poor direct blood supply
options.D: Ligaments are made of bone tissue which cannot regenerate

explanation: Spot on! Ligaments have very few blood vessels running through them, meaning healing nutrients take much longer to arrive. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T5#GNS121_U3_T5_h8)

question: Which symptom is a major red flag for Meniere's disease?

options.A: Sudden complete ear pain
options.B: Bleeding from the ear canal
options.C: Purulent ear discharge
options.D: Episodic vertigo

explanation: Spot on! Meniere's disease causes sudden, severe spells of spinning dizziness (vertigo), along with ringing in the ears and hearing changes. [learn more](GNS311_U3_T5#GNS311_U3_T5_h3)

question: Why is it strictly forbidden to press down or compress waste bags by hand?

options.A: It destroys the municipal recycling value of paper packaging
options.B: It increases the weight beyond what the utility trolley can carry
options.C: Compression causes the plastic material to dissolve into toxic fumes
options.D: Hidden needles or sharps can puncture the bag and cause injury

explanation: Spot on! Pressing down on bags is a fast way to get pricked by hidden sharps. Never compress your waste bags! [learn more](GST114_U6_T5#GST114_U6_T5_h5)

question: A dying patient says they are scared to die alone while family steps out. What should you do?

options.A: Tell them not to worry because family will be back tomorrow
options.B: Sit with them and offer a reassuring, calming presence
options.C: Run out to find the doctor right away
options.D: Tell them to think about happier times

explanation: Sometimes your physical presence is the best medicine. Just staying by their side chases away that terrifying loneliness. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T3#GNS221_U4_T3_h8)

question: What type of cleaning technique should a nurse use for skeletal traction pin sites?

options.A: Routine household washing
options.B: Clean technique
options.C: Sterile technique
options.D: Surgical scrubbing without gloves

explanation: Because those pins go straight into the bone, keeping things sterile is a must to stop germs from causing a bone infection. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T12#GNS221_U1_T12_h6)

question: Why do public health nurses track family planning statistics?

options.A: To calculate exact hospital budgets for surgery
options.B: To punish communities with high birth rates
options.C: To replace direct physical assessment of patients
options.D: To track reproductive trends and measure health policies

explanation: Think of family planning stats as your community's report card! They help nurses and public health workers spot health trends and see if our policies are actually helping women and families. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T027#GNS226_U6_T027_h1)

question: Why must you always inspect the tip of an IV catheter after you remove it?

options.A: To determine what gauge size was used for the infusion
options.B: To measure the exact length of the vein inside the client's arm
options.C: To ensure the catheter tip broke off completely or remained intact
options.D: To check if any blood clots formed inside the plastic tubing

explanation: Always double-check that tiny plastic tip! Ensuring it's in one piece means no broken plastic fragment floated off into the patient's bloodstream. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T17#GNS122_U1_T17_h7)

question: Why should a nurse keep a patient's cultural background in mind when assessing grief?

options.A: Cultural background is the only factor that influences grieving speed
options.B: Cultural beliefs determine the exact physical symptoms of grief in the body
options.C: Culture prevents people from ever experiencing complicated grief
options.D: Culture dictates how people appropriately express and ritualize mourning

explanation: Spot on! Different cultures have unique ways of mourning and showing sadness. Respecting this helps you give truly patient-centered care. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T5#GNS221_U4_T5_h5)

question: What is an essential nursing check after a patient has surgery on their fallopian tubes?

options.A: Measuring hand grip strength in both arms
options.B: Checking for active bowel sounds in the chest
options.C: Monitoring vital signs closely for internal bleeding
options.D: Testing the patient's eyesight every hour

explanation: Any surgery near pelvic blood vessels carries a risk of bleeding, so keeping a close eye on vital signs helps catch complications early. Proud of your daily progress! [learn more](GNS216_U5_T25#GNS216_U5_T25_h6)

question: Which device is best for giving tiny amounts of medicine slowly over time, especially for newborns?

options.A: Ambulatory blood warmer
options.B: Gravity drip set
options.C: Large volume pump
options.D: Syringe pump

explanation: Great job! Syringe pumps are brilliant for low volumes because they push the plunger forward in tiny, steady steps. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T3#GNS212_U4_T3_h2)

question: When would you choose a face mask instead of a nasal cannula for oxygen delivery?

options.A: When the patient only requires a very low flow rate of oxygen
options.B: When the patient refuses to have anything touching their face
options.C: When the patient is completely free of any respiratory distress
options.D: When the patient needs higher and more precise oxygen concentrations

explanation: Face masks cover both the nose and mouth, making them the go-to choice when a patient in distress needs a stronger, concentrated flow of oxygen. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T11#GNS212_U2_T11_h1)

question: What system do water-soluble hormones use to pass along messages inside a cell?

options.A: Direct nuclear transcription
options.B: Intracellular cholesterol
options.C: Second messenger systems
options.D: Direct DNA replication

explanation: Since water-soluble hormones can't enter the cell themselves, they drop their message off at the surface, triggering a 'second messenger' inside the cell to carry out the orders. [learn more](GNS211_U1_T10#GNS211_U1_T10_h7)

question: Which inner layer of the joint capsule is responsible for making synovial fluid?

options.A: The outer reinforcing ligament band
options.B: The outer fibrous capsule layer
options.C: The glassy articular cartilage pad
options.D: The inner synovial membrane

explanation: Brilliant! The inner lining is the synovial membrane—it acts like a little factory that secretes that slippery fluid. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T6#GNS121_U3_T6_h5)

question: Why is good communication especially critical in busy primary health clinics?

options.A: It prevents dangerous mistakes caused by misunderstood instructions
options.B: It removes the need for doctors in the clinic
options.C: It allows the nurse to spend less time working with patients
options.D: It completely stops patients from seeking traditional healers

explanation: When clinics are crowded and resources are stretched, clear communication ensures patients still understand their medications and care instructions, avoiding serious errors. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T12#GNS124_U5_T12_h1)

question: Which common pregnancy complication is closely linked to widespread placental infarctions (tissue death)?

options.A: Gestational diabetes
options.B: Preeclampsia
options.C: Hyperemesis gravidarum
options.D: Iron deficiency anemia

explanation: High blood pressure disorders like preeclampsia narrow the tiny blood vessels in the placenta, cutting off proper blood flow and causing small areas of tissue to die. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T6#GNS121_U6_T6_h5)

question: Why does severe pain after belly surgery put a patient at risk for lung problems like atelectasis?

options.A: Inflammation travels straight from the belly to the lungs
options.B: High blood pressure fills the lungs with fluid
options.C: Patients take shallow breaths and avoid coughing to protect their stitches
options.D: Pain meds paralyze the breathing muscles

explanation: When it hurts to move your tummy, you naturally take shallow breaths. This prevents deep breaths, causing tiny air sacs in the lungs to collapse. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T2#GNS123_U3_T2_h7)

question: In advanced breast cancer, what causes that dimpled 'peau d'orange' (orange peel) skin texture?

options.A: Blockage of the dermal lymphatic vessels by cancer cells
options.B: An allergic reaction to topical herbal ointments
options.C: Bacterial infection of the superficial sweat glands
options.D: Severe dehydration leading to dry skin flaking

explanation: When cancer cells block the tiny lymph channels in the skin, fluid backs up and creates that bumpy, orange-peel look. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T9#GNS313_U3_T9_h5)

question: A patient suddenly feels dizzy, sweaty, and pale during a proctoscopy. What should you, as the nurse, do immediately?

options.A: Ask the patient to stand up and walk around the room
options.B: Administer an oral laxative to clear remaining stool
options.C: Encourage the patient to push harder to finish the test
options.D: Stop the procedure immediately and notify the clinician

explanation: Safety first! These are classic signs of a vasovagal faint. Always pause the procedure right away and get help to keep your patient safe. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T7#GNS221_U2_T7_h5)

question: Why do community nurses still use paper records and stationery instead of computers all the time?

options.A: Community outposts often lack reliable computer networks and digital infrastructure
options.B: Paper forms are legally required to be more accurate than digital files
options.C: Rural patients refuse to let nurses use computers near them
options.D: Computers cannot store health data related to immunization

explanation: Spot on! Because remote health posts and home visits rarely have steady electricity or internet, good old paper remains our most practical tool. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T13#GNS225_U2_T13_h1)

question: What emotional care is essential for a woman recovering from a scary birth emergency?

options.A: Emotional debriefing and supportive counseling about the traumatic event
options.B: Immediate transfer to a psychiatric institution for sedation
options.C: Complete isolation from family members to ensure physical rest
options.D: Strict avoidance of talking about the childbirth experience

explanation: Birth emergencies can be terrifying. A listening ear and compassionate counseling help mothers heal both inside and out. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T009#GNS226_U1_T009_h8)

question: What is the best way to determine if a patient is ready to discuss serious health information?

options.A: Ask for their permission and check what they already know
options.B: Wait until the family demands an update from the doctor
options.C: Assume they want all details because they are in the hospital
options.D: Read the entire medical history before speaking to them

explanation: Asking permission and checking current understanding respects the patient's personal pacing and avoids overwhelming them. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T6#GNS321_U4_T6_h3)

question: What causes the initial change in charge when an action potential starts in a neuron?

options.A: Potassium ions leave the cell permanently
options.B: Calcium ions are stored in the nucleus
options.C: Sodium ions rush into the cell
options.D: Neurotransmitters dissolve the cell membrane

explanation: The opening of sodium channels allows positive sodium ions to flood inward, reversing the membrane charge. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T1#GNS222_U3_T1_h6)

question: A patient is given naloxone to wake them up and reverse a dangerous morphine overdose. What kind of drug action is this?

options.A: Absorption
options.B: Potentiation
options.C: Antagonism
options.D: Synergism

explanation: Spot on! Naloxone acts as a true antagonist—it rushes to the rescue, kicks the morphine off the receptors, and blocks its effects to save the patient. [learn more](GNS215_U2_T4#GNS215_U2_T4_h3)

question: What is the proper technique for pulling a peripheral IV cannula out of a patient's skin?

question: What is a major benefit of good teamwork and communication on a ward?

options.A: It eliminates the need for patient medical records

options.C: It allows the ward to close earlier every evening
options.D: It helps prevent medical errors and streamlines treatment

explanation: Spot on! When doctors, nurses, and other health workers talk clearly, everyone stays on the same page and mistakes are easily avoided. [learn more](GST321_U6_T2#GST321_U6_T2_h7)

question: Where in the brain is the main control center that keeps your breathing rhythm on autopilot?

options.A: Hypothalamus and pituitary gland
options.B: Medulla oblongata and pons
options.C: Cerebrum and cerebral cortex
options.D: Cerebellum and spinal cord

explanation: Correct! The brainstem quietly manages your breathing rhythm in the background so you don't have to think about it. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T1#GNS213_U2_T1_h6)

question: How should a nurse document what a patient says about experiencing abuse?

options.A: Write a generalized summary to protect family privacy

options.C: Leave the information out of the chart to prevent legal complications
options.D: Record only the nursing diagnosis without patient comments

question: What is the primary characteristic of a generic drug name?

options.A: It is exclusively owned and trademarked by one manufacturing company

options.C: It changes depending on which country the medication is imported from
options.D: It describes the exact atomic arrangement of the chemical structure

explanation: The generic name is the universal, public name given to the active drug, no matter who manufactures it. Think of it as the drug's true identity! [learn more](GNS125_U1_T8#GNS125_U1_T8_h2)

question: What term is used for the time it takes for half of a hormone to be cleared from the bloodstream?

options.A: Degradation time

options.C: Clearance factor
options.D: Half-life

question: Why does money collected from selling drugs in a DRF go right back into the fund instead of a general government account?

options.A: To ensure the money is immediately available to buy more drug stock
options.B: To pay off international government debts and loans
options.C: To cover the cost of unrelated building construction projects
options.D: To pay the personal salaries of the hospital management team

explanation: You got it! Keeping the money right where it is (ring-fencing it) ensures the pharmacy can restock quickly without waiting for government bureaucracy. [learn more](GNS215_U3_T2#GNS215_U3_T2_h1)

question: Why do community nurses need to collaborate with other professionals when solving health problems?

options.A: It reduces the cost of running primary healthcare clinics
options.B: It ensures that doctors make all decisions without community input
options.C: Complex health problems require diverse skills and coordinated efforts
options.D: It eliminates the need for nurses to conduct home visits

explanation: Spot on! Because health is tied to housing, water, and social life, different professionals have to team up to find real solutions. [learn more](GNS225_U1_T8#GNS225_U1_T8_h7)

question: A patient is given a drug that blocks parasympathetic activity. Which symptom would you most likely see?

options.A: Rapid digestion and frequent urination

options.C: Dry mouth and decreased bowel sounds
options.D: Constricted pupils and low blood pressure

question: What safety advice should a nurse give a patient discharged with a drowsy anti-nausea drug like promethazine?

options.A: Avoid driving or operating heavy machinery until the drug's effects are known

options.C: Increase dietary fiber to prevent sudden high blood pressure
options.D: Take the medication exclusively on an empty stomach with milk

explanation: Correct! Many antiemetics make you sleepy, so patient safety means warning them away from driving until they know how the drug affects them. Wonderful patient education! [learn more](GNS223_U3_T6#GNS223_U3_T6_h8)

question: What is usually the first sign that makes a patient say, 'I need to get this cough checked out'?

options.A: A persistent, worsening cough
options.B: Sudden complete blindness
options.C: Inability to swallow food
options.D: Severe lower abdominal pain

question: What causes the first heart sound, commonly heard as 'lub'?

options.D: Closing of the AV valves

question: Which of these is a classic example of an open drainage system?

options.B: Hemovac evacuator
options.C: Penrose drain
options.D: Foley catheter bag

question: What is a quick, drug-free comfort measure you can teach a patient for crampy pelvic pain?

options.A: Engaging in high-intensity aerobic exercise
options.B: Consuming high amounts of caffeine
options.C: Applying ice packs directly to the pelvic region
options.D: Applying local heat therapy to the lower abdomen

question: Which major sense skips the thalamus relay station and goes straight to the cortex?

options.A: Vision
options.B: Touch

question: What is Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia (BPH)?

options.A: A bacterial infection inside the seminal vesicles
options.B: A complete absence of bulbourethral secretions
options.C: A malignant tumor spreading from the testes
options.D: A non-cancerous enlargement of the prostate gland

question: What is the primary function of a hospital journal club?

options.A: To help nurses read, discuss, and understand research articles together
options.B: To discipline nurses who make mistakes during procedures
options.C: To write brand new research papers for international publishing
options.D: To raise money for buying new ward equipment

question: Which option best describes true informed consent in clinical research?

options.A: An agreement signed by the hospital manager on behalf of the patients
options.B: A verbal promise made by the researcher that no complications will occur
options.C: An ongoing, voluntary dialogue ensuring participants understand risks and rights

explanation: Informed consent isn't just a one-time signature. It's a continuous conversation making sure the participant is fully aware and knows they can walk away anytime. [learn more](GNS217_U2_T5#GNS217_U2_T5_h4)

question: What common barrier often affects contraceptive uptake in resource-constrained Nigerian communities?

options.A: Universal preference for large families exceeding ten children
options.B: Financial constraints and out-of-pocket supply costs
options.C: An absolute lack of any modern contraceptive methods globally
options.D: Laws that ban nurses from discussing birth control openly

question: A young patient comes in with a racing heart, high blood pressure, and extreme agitation after taking a street drug. Which category is most likely at play?

options.A: Cannabinoids
options.B: Sedatives
options.C: Stimulants
options.D: Depressants

question: What happens in the body during the resistance stage of stress?

options.A: The sympathetic nervous system shuts down completely
options.B: Energy reserves are fully depleted and the person collapses
options.C: The body attempts to adapt and cope with the ongoing stressor
options.D: No hormonal or physiological changes take place

question: What approach matters most when doing a physical assessment on an FGM survivor?

options.A: Insisting that family members stay in the room to answer questions

options.C: Trauma-informed care that prioritizes patient dignity and consent

question: A patient has been dealing with severe chronic financial and physical stress for over a year and now has a failing immune system and frequent infections. Which stage of GAS are they experiencing?

options.A: Stage of resistance
options.B: Homeostatic baseline stage
options.C: Stage of exhaustion
options.D: Alarm reaction stage

question: Which special cell type must be present to diagnose Hodgkin Lymphoma?

options.A: Epithelial cells
options.B: Reed-Sternberg cells
options.C: Plasma cells
options.D: Kupffer cells

question: Why should you check for bladder fullness using a scanner or your hands before placing a catheter?

options.A: To numb the urethral canal before inserting the tube

question: Why must you check a patient's kidney function before they get an injection of contrast dye?

options.A: Contrast dye increases the daily urine output significantly
options.B: Poor kidney function prevents the dye from reaching the joints
options.C: Kidneys must filter the dye to make bones show up white
options.D: Contrast dye can be toxic to the kidneys if clearance is slow

explanation: The kidneys have to filter out contrast dye. If a patient's kidneys aren't working well, the dye can linger and cause kidney damage, so checking lab results first is a crucial nursing duty. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T4#GNS222_U1_T4_h7)

question: You want to launch an immunization campaign in a rural village. Which approach shows a great BCC strategy?

options.A: Posting English warning signs in markets where people cannot read English
options.B: Waiting quietly at the clinic for patients to walk in by themselves
options.C: Partnering with local women's groups and trusted peer educators for dialogue
options.D: Publishing dense medical research papers in international journals

explanation: Brilliant choice! Working with trusted local groups and talking face-to-face always beats sitting back and waiting or using confusing posters. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T3#GNS124_U5_T3_h3)

question: A patient taking gliclazide is awake but looks shaky, sweaty, and confused. What is your best immediate nursing action?

options.A: Wait patiently for thirty minutes to see if symptoms pass
options.B: Inject a large dose of long-acting insulin subcutaneously
options.C: Administer 15 grams of fast-acting oral carbohydrates
options.D: Encourage the patient to go for a brisk walk to burn energy

explanation: You got it! Giving quick sugar (like juice or a glucose tablet) safely raises their blood sugar and fixes those scary early symptoms fast. [learn more](GNS223_U7_T1#GNS223_U7_T1_h6)

question: Why shouldn't you rely purely on personal opinion in a nursing paper?

options.A: Instructors simply do not like reading personal thoughts
options.B: Clinical claims must rest on verifiable evidence
options.C: Personal opinions are always grammatically incorrect
options.D: It takes too much time to write out opinions

explanation: Spot on! Nursing is an evidence-based field, meaning we always back our care with proven facts rather than just guesswork. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T7#GNS217_U3_T7_h1)

question: What is the primary job of the hormone relaxin during pregnancy?

options.A: To loosen ligaments and joints, especially in the pelvis
options.B: To calm the digestive tract and reduce morning sickness
options.C: To soften the amniotic sac and prevent premature rupture
options.D: To relax the airways and improve maternal oxygen intake

explanation: Relaxin lives up to its name! It relaxes and softens the body's connective tissues to get the pelvis ready for the baby to pass through during birth. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T14#GNS121_U5_T14_h6)

question: How can nurses help solve scheduling problems caused by traditional family and caregiving duties?

options.A: By offering clinic hours that accommodate domestic responsibilities
options.B: By charging extra fees for patients who arrive late
options.C: By refusing to treat patients who have caregiving duties
options.D: By keeping clinics open only during standard morning work hours

explanation: Flexible clinic timings make it possible for people juggling heavy caregiving duties to still get the medical care they need. Wonderful thinking! [learn more](GNS225_U5_T22#GNS225_U5_T22_h8)

question: Why must patients taking bulk-forming laxatives drink plenty of water with them?

options.A: To activate the chemical formula in the liver first
options.B: To stop the kidneys from producing too much urine
options.C: To prevent the drug from absorbing into the bloodstream
options.D: To prevent the supplement from swelling and blocking the throat or bowel

explanation: Without enough water, bulk-forming agents can absorb moisture from the esophagus or intestines and cause a dangerous blockage. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T6#GNS212_U1_T6_h5)

question: When should a wound culture specimen ideally be collected?

options.A: Before starting any antimicrobial therapy
options.B: Immediately after applying a medicated ointment
options.C: After the patient finishes their antibiotic course
options.D: Only when the laboratory technician arrives on the ward

explanation: Collecting cultures before starting drugs ensures the active pathogen is present and not suppressed by medication. [learn more](GST114_U1_T3#GST114_U1_T3_h5)

question: Why should a nurse manager figure out the exact type of conflict happening?

options.A: To decide which nurse should be fired
options.B: To punish the staff members involved
options.C: To pinpoint the true source of friction
options.D: To fulfill mandatory hospital paperwork

explanation: Spotting the right category helps leaders fix the actual root cause instead of just treating surface drama. Spot on! [learn more](GST321_U5_T3#GST321_U5_T3_h1)

question: A patient has a stiff, painful knee joint. Which membrane inside the joint is likely failing to produce enough lubricating fluid?

options.A: Cutaneous membrane
options.B: Synovial membrane
options.C: Serous membrane
options.D: Mucous membrane

explanation: Synovial membranes line our movable joints and pump out synovial fluid to keep movements smooth and pain-free. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T8#GNS111_U1_T8_h6)

question: Which of these is NOT a common fetal complication linked to untreated hyperemesis?

options.A: Intestinal growth restriction
options.B: Low birth weight
options.C: Congenital heart murmurs
options.D: Preterm birth

explanation: Heart defects happen during early structural development, whereas hyperemesis baby issues are usually about poor nutrition and low birth weight. You're mastering neonatal risks! [learn more](GNS226_U2_T016#GNS226_U2_T016_h4)

question: Why is checking a patient's 'functional vision' so helpful when planning their daily nursing care?

options.A: It shows what the patient can actually see and do in daily life.
options.B: It determines the exact medical cause of the eye disease.
options.C: It changes the official hospital diagnosis code.
options.D: It proves whether the patient needs surgery immediately.

explanation: Brilliant! Functional vision looks at practical everyday abilities rather than just clinical numbers, helping us figure out the best ways to support their independence. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T13#GNS324_U4_T13_h1)

question: What directly causes barotrauma in a patient on a ventilator?

options.A: Lack of early physical therapy and leg movement
options.B: Inadequate hand hygiene by the nursing staff
options.C: Bacterial infection growing in the endotracheal tube
options.D: High airway pressure or excessive lung volume

explanation: Too much pressure or blowing the lungs up like an over-inflated balloon can pop delicate air sacs, causing air to leak where it shouldn't. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T10#GNS321_U2_T10_h6)
